Tinubu made the remark on Saturday at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Ibadan, Oyo State, in what appeared to be a veiled reference to the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), the political platform adopted by Governor Seyi Makinde for his 2027 presidential ambition.
Tinubu Guarantees Improved Electricity, Unveils Deal To Revive Leyland Factory
Although the President did not mention Makinde or the APM by name, his comments came amid the governor’s decision to contest the 2027 presidential election on the platform of the party.
“We heard there is a certain group/faction called the ‘Palẹmọ’ (Pack up) group. Don’t mind them; they are only waiting in vain; there is nowhere they are going,” Tinubu said.
Makinde had declared his presidential ambition under the APM and subsequently accepted the party’s nomination, promising to reset Nigeria if elected.
The President’s remark at the Ibadan rally, held in the governor’s home state, appeared to be directed at the emerging political opposition ahead of the 2027 general election.
Tinubu, who was in Oyo State to canvass support for his re-election bid, urged party supporters to remain committed to the APC and its political agenda.
He thanked residents of the state for their support, insisting that continuity in governance was necessary to sustain ongoing reforms and secure a prosperous future for Nigerians.
“I just want to say thank you, thank you for all you have been doing and all the support you have given to APC. APC is our party. It is your party,” he said.
“You must stay the course. You must, for the sake of progress, prosperity of our country, development for your children and our great-grandchildren.”
